question: Six regrets people describe. Which kind fades with the years, and which still stings decades later?
answer: The things not done last. Gilovich and Medvec found actions hurt more at first, but over a lifetime regrets of inaction dominate. People repair a mistake or find its silver lining; a missed chance has no ending, and the reasons that held them back fade faster than the dream.
move: Ask which choice you would still be explaining in twenty years.
ask: Which choice facing me now will I still be explaining in twenty years if I do not make it?

items.note: Took a job that turned out badly.
items.verdict: Actions get explained: at least it showed what I did not want.

items.note: Never asked out the person they liked.
items.verdict: No answer ever came, so the imagined one stays perfect.

items.note: Sent something embarrassing late at night.
items.verdict: Sharp for a week. Then it turns into a story told against yourself.

items.note: Never went back to finish their education.
items.verdict: Education tops the lists of what people regret most in later life.

items.note: Bought a car that was a mistake.
items.verdict: Sold, written off, forgotten. A mistake made can be repaired.

items.note: Always meant to travel, and never did.
items.verdict: With time the obstacles shrink in memory, and the trip not taken grows.

reference: Gilovich and Medvec, The Experience of Regret: What, When, and Why, Psychological Review 102:379, 1995; Roese and Summerville, What We Regret Most... and Why, Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin 31:1273, 2005
